source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); WORKSHEET - Standard Deduction for People 65 or Older and/or Blind (PDF page 6); FILING STATUS (PDF page 6): 'If your federal filing status is Qualifying Widow(er) with Dependent Child, check the Head of Household box'; tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 6,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 40,000.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 40,000.00 + (0.00) = 40,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (qualifying surviving spouse, Head of Household box on the K-40), worksheet for people 65 or older: 1 box checked, 6,180.00 + 1 x 850.00 = 7,030.00 (the worksheet prints 7,030.00); line 5 exemption allowance 9,160.00 + head of household additional exemption 2,320.00 = 11,480.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 7,030.00 + 11,480.00 = 18,510.00; line 7 taxable income = 40,000.00 - 18,510.00 = 21,490.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 21,490.00 = 1,117.4800 = 1,117.48. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 21,451-21,500, single, head of household or married filing separate column, PDF page 28, gives 1,117; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 1,117.48. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 1,117.48. Kansas treats this status as Head of Household, so the step is 850.00 (the head of household line of the worksheet), although the federal amount here uses the married 1,600.00 and the projection's bracket schedule is joint. Taxable income is under 23,000, so the bracket approximation does not change the tax. No dependents in the inputs; the form would add 2,320.00 per dependent.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
The blind amount, dependent exemptions and disabled veteran exemption are not applied (not_modelled).
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
